title.es: Episodio de pódcast: escuchar, resumir, responder

es: Escuchar un episodio de pódcast, resumirlo con fidelidad, señalar una implicación y añadir una reacción propia con matiz.

teaching.en: In this episode, the host asked her guest about working from home.
teaching.es: En este episodio, la presentadora preguntó a su invitado por el teletrabajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Se resume quién preguntó y a quién: host y guest organizan el episodio.
segments: In this episode, the host asked
her guest about working from home.

teaching.en: What struck me was that the guest never said the job was easy.
teaching.es: Lo que me llamó la atención fue que el invitado nunca dijo que el trabajo fuera fácil.
teaching.explanationEs: What struck me was… introduce lo que te llamó la atención, incluso lo no dicho.
segments: What struck me was that the guest
never said the job was easy.
teaching.audioText: What struck me was that the guest never said the job was easy.

teaching.en: She did not say it, but her answer seemed to imply that the change was hard.
teaching.es: No lo dijo, pero su respuesta parecía dar a entender que el cambio era difícil.
teaching.explanationEs: Seemed to imply señala una implicación sin afirmarla.

seemed to imply that the change was hard.

teaching.en: To be fair, the idea is good, but I would add one doubt; the guest would probably agree.
teaching.es: Para ser justos, la idea es buena, pero yo añadiría una duda; el invitado probablemente estaría de acuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: To be fair reconoce lo bueno; I would add suma un punto propio.

teaching.es: Mi primera reacción fue estar de acuerdo con ella hasta cierto punto.
teaching.explanationEs: Up to a point matiza el acuerdo: no es total.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que resume lo que dijo la invitada, sin opinar.

choices.text: The guest said that some people feel lonely at home.
The guest is wrong about feeling lonely.
I think that nobody feels lonely at home.

feedback.es: Un resumen fiel repite lo dicho con un verbo de reporte; las otras frases añaden una opinión.

hint.es: Un resumen fiel repite lo que dijo, sin tu opinión.

origin.text: Guest: Some people feel lonely when they work from home.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que me llamó la atención fue su sinceridad.»

feedback.es: Struck es el pasado de strike: what struck me = lo que me llamó la atención.

hint.es: Es el verbo de la clase para algo que te llama la atención.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con su función en el comentario.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula ocupa un lugar: resumir, insinuar, matizar o añadir una opinión propia.

hint.es: Piensa si cada fórmula habla de lo dicho, de lo insinuado o de tu opinión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la invitada sobre el museo.

choices.text: That the museum is free on Sundays.
That visiting it may not be worth the trouble.
That the museum is closed at weekends.

feedback.es: Con «Well…», «a bit pricey» y una cola larga en fin de semana, la invitada insinúa que quizá no compensa ir.

origin.audio: Host: Is the new museum worth a visit? Guest: Well… the tickets are a bit pricey, and the queue is long at weekends.

choices.text: Shared offices are a disaster.
The guest is right about everything.
To be fair, the price is an advantage; however, I would add that teams need to meet sometimes.

feedback.es: Reconoce lo bueno con to be fair y añade una duda con however: es una reacción matizada.

origin.text: Guest: Shared offices are cheaper, but some teams say they feel less close.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me sorprendió que sonara tan segura.»

answer.text: I was surprised that she sounded so sure

feedback.es: I was surprised that + oración expresa sorpresa ante lo dicho.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y escribe un resumen con una implicación y tu reacción.

answer.text: In this episode, the host asked her guest whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. First, many people save about two hours a day because they do not travel, and this is a real benefit. Second, some workers feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. Third, she said that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a good compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced. However, I would add one doubt: not everybody has a quiet room at home, so the benefits may be smaller for some people. I see her point, but I would like to hear more before I decide. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I agree with her up to a point.

In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I agree with her up to a point.

This episode of the podcast was about working from home. The host asked her guest if it is better, and the guest explained that it depends. On the positive side, many people save two hours a day because they do not travel to an office. On the negative side, some of them feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. She suggested that a good compromise could be two office days a week. The host asked again whether working at home is better, and the guest replied not exactly, which implied that the situation is more complicated than a simple yes or no. My reaction is positive: to be fair, she did not try to sell one answer. What struck me was how honest she was about the problems. However, I would add that some people do not have a quiet place at home, and that could make things harder for them. Overall, I agree with her up to a point, and I would like to hear how companies respond.

feedback.es: El texto resume lo dicho con fidelidad, detecta la implicación de «not exactly», reacciona con matiz y cierra con una conclusión.

origin.text: Escucha el episodio (puedes oírlo varias veces) y escribe en inglés, de 160 a 300 palabras, una reseña: resume las ideas de la invitada (atribúyelas), señala una implicación, añade tu reacción con un matiz (to be fair, I would add…) y termina con una frase de cierre. No inventes datos.
origin.audio: Host: Welcome to the show. Today my guest studies working from home. Is it better to work at home? Guest: Well, it depends. Many people save two hours a day because they do not travel, and that is a real benefit. Host: So it is better? Guest: Not exactly. Some people tell me they feel lonely, and they hardly see their colleagues. Host: Is there a solution? Guest: Perhaps. Companies could offer two office days a week, and I suppose that is a good compromise. Host: Thank you for joining us.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que quiere decir la invitada.

choices.text: The plan did not really work.
The plan was a great success.
The plan has not started yet.

feedback.es: «Not exactly a success, to be honest» es una forma suave de decir que el plan no funcionó.

origin.audio: Host: Did the plan work? Guest: Well… it was not exactly a success, to be honest.

feedback.es: Hang on frena la conversación antes de sorry to interrupt.

choices.text: A photo when the listener arrives.
A short call when the listener arrives.
A letter when the listener arrives.

feedback.es: En el inglés de Nigeria, flash me pide una llamada rápida al llegar.

origin.text: My colleague from Nigeria says: «Flash me when you arrive.»

prompt.es: Elige la frase que distingue lo dicho de tu opinión.

choices.text: According to me, the guest thinks offices help teams.
The guest thinks that I think offices are not necessary.
According to the guest, offices help teams; in my view, they are not always necessary.

feedback.es: Atribuye la idea con according to y separa tu punto de vista con in my view.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para ser justos, el episodio fue equilibrado.»

answer.text: To be fair the episode was balanced

feedback.es: To be fair abre la frase para reconocer un mérito.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la invitada.

choices.text: She doubts that the company will agree.
She is sure the company will agree.
She has not heard the proposal.

feedback.es: «We will see» y «I hardly think» muestran que duda de que la empresa acepte.

origin.audio: Guest: We will see, but I hardly think the company will agree.
